applicabilityBasis.summary: DUSD is a transferable dollar-targeted CDP stablecoin created against posted collateral. Alto explicitly accepts it as payment for reward-option exercises and permits circulation beyond its markets. Its public USDC swap facility is inventory-limited, charges fees and is administratively pausable. Alto also expressly denies an obligation to repurchase or redeem DUSD for any consideration. These documented payment uses and contrary redemption terms create a genuine payment-stablecoin applicability ambiguity under GENIUS section 2(22); a swap into USDC alone does not establish an obligation to redeem for currency or bank-deposit monetary value.

genius.notes: This is a sourced assessment of documented scope ambiguity, not an authorization or statutory-exclusion finding. Alto Foundation is identified as a Cayman Islands foundation company that deployed and provides protocol software. Mesh Interface Corp. is identified as the separate Panama front-end operator. Neither role is treated as evidence that the entity is a legal DUSD payment-stablecoin issuer or monetary-redemption obligor, so issuerEntity and issuerDomicile are omitted. The Owner Safe, Timelock and emergency controls prevent assuming Liquity-style immutability or a fully decentralized no-issuer design. Payment use is expressly documented, so the CDP label and no-redemption disclaimer do not support a categorical non-payment-token classification. Public GENIUS authorization posture and issuer pathway remain unresolved. No no-public-authorization-found status, enforcement finding, reserve-disclosure flag or attestation finding is asserted from the bounded searches. This treatment follows the unclear-applicability convention for LUSD, GHO and crvUSD without importing their separate negative-authorization reviews.
